title: Generated columns (virtual by default in PG 18, vs STORED) and exclusion constraints
summary: A generated column derives its value from the rest of the row: virtual (the PG 18 default) computes it on read, STORED on write. Exclusion constraints generalize UNIQUE to other operators, so "no two bookings overlap" becomes a declaration.

examples.title: A virtual and a stored generated column side by side

annotations.note: No keyword means VIRTUAL in PG 18: no storage, computed whenever the column is read, like a column of a view. PG 12 to 17 had only stored generated columns and required the STORED keyword, so DDL written without it is PG 18+ only.

STORED computes the value on INSERT and UPDATE and writes it to disk: it costs space and write time, reads are free, and it can be indexed. Either kind may use only immutable functions and the current row: no subqueries, no other generated columns.
The INSERT never mentions the generated columns, and the UPDATE of vat_pct changes gross_cents with no trigger. Writing one yourself fails with SQLSTATE 428C9: cannot insert a non-DEFAULT value.

lower('Iğdır') gives 'iğdır' under the database's C.UTF-8 rules, not the Turkish 'ığdır'. lower(name COLLATE "tr-x-icu") is allowed in a generation expression and gives 'ığdır'. A STORED column bakes the rules in at write time. Also note gross_cents: integer division truncates, so put the rounding rule into the expression.
pg_attribute.attgenerated tells the kinds apart: 'v' virtual, 's' stored, empty for ordinary columns.

The stored column takes a normal B-tree index. PG 18 rejects an index on a virtual column (SQLSTATE 0A000), and also a UNIQUE constraint on one. To index such a value, make it STORED or index the expression itself.

examples.title: EXCLUDE ... WITH &&: no two bookings overlap

annotations.note: A real schema would use tstzrange (see the time zones lesson). tsrange keeps the printed output independent of the session's time zone.

For any two rows, during && during must not be true. A B-tree can only answer equality and ordering, so overlap needs a GiST index, which the constraint creates. Range types bring their own GiST support: no extension needed.
Half-open ranges [start, end) make back-to-back bookings legal: one ends at 10:00, the next starts at 10:00, and they share no instant. With a closed upper bound, 10:00 would belong to both.
11:00 to 12:00 overlaps Mehmet's booking, so the insert fails with SQLSTATE 23P01 (exclusion_violation). A UNIQUE constraint can't express this: the two ranges are not equal.

examples.title: Per room, live bookings only: = and && with btree_gist

annotations.note: btree_gist adds GiST support for scalar types such as text and int. Without it the CREATE TABLE fails: data type text has no default operator class for access method "gist". CREATE EXTENSION is transactional, so here it is rolled back with everything else; a real database installs it once, in a migration.
Two rows conflict only when room = room AND during && during. The WHERE clause makes the constraint partial: cancelled bookings don't take part, which no UNIQUE constraint can express.
Same time, different rooms: the = comparison is false, so there is no conflict.
Cancelling booking 1 takes it out of the constraint, so booking 3 can claim an overlapping slot in Galata.
10:00 to 11:00 overlaps booking 3 (09:30 to 10:30) in the same room, so the insert fails with SQLSTATE 23P01.

use_cases: STORED: normalized lookup keys such as lower(name) or a slug that you filter or sort on and must index
VIRTUAL: derived values read now and then, such as gross from net and VAT, display names or unit conversions
EXCLUDE: room and resource booking, non-overlapping validity periods for prices or tax rates, one active assignment per person at a time
strengths: Unlike a computed property on a Go struct or a TS class, the value is the same for every reader: reports, other services and psql
A virtual column costs no storage, and adding one never rewrites the table (adding a STORED one does)
An exclusion constraint replaces the application's 'look for an overlap, then insert', which races: two concurrent overlapping inserts can't both commit
weaknesses: PG 18 can't index virtual columns or put UNIQUE on them; anything you search by needs STORED or an expression index
Virtual columns may use only built-in functions and types, and are recomputed on every read
Changing a STORED column's expression (ALTER COLUMN ... SET EXPRESSION) rewrites its existing data
Exclusion constraints need a GiST index, btree_gist for = on scalar columns, and can't be arbiters for ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE

pitfalls.title: Indexing a virtual column
pitfalls.detail: In PG 18 a generated column without a keyword is virtual, and CREATE INDEX on it fails with 'indexes on virtual generated columns are not supported'. Decide the kind when you create the column.
pitfalls.bad: name_key text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (lower(name))  -- then CREATE INDEX ... (name_key)
pitfalls.good: name_key text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (lower(name)) STORED

pitfalls.title: Closed ranges for back-to-back slots
pitfalls.detail: '[09:00,10:00]' and '[10:00,11:00)' overlap at 10:00, so the second booking is rejected. Use half-open '[)' ranges, which is also what tsrange(a, b) builds by default.

pitfalls.title: Forgetting btree_gist
pitfalls.detail: EXCLUDE USING gist (room WITH =, ...) on a text or int column needs the btree_gist extension. It is trusted, so the database owner can install it without superuser rights.

pitfalls.title: Case rules frozen into a stored key
pitfalls.detail: A STORED lower(name) is computed with the rules in force at write time. Under C.UTF-8, 'IĞDIR' becomes 'iğdir'. If Turkish rules matter, write lower(name COLLATE "tr-x-icu") in the expression.

quiz.q: In PG 18, what does `total int GENERATED ALWAYS AS (price * qty)` (no keyword) create?
quiz.why: Virtual is the default in PG 18. PG 12 to 17 required the STORED keyword, so they reject this line.

quiz.q: Which generated column can you index in PG 18?
quiz.why: Indexes on virtual generated columns are not supported in PG 18; a stored one indexes like any other column.

quiz.q: Bookings '[09:00,10:00)' and '[10:00,11:00)' in the same room, with EXCLUDE USING gist (room WITH =, during WITH &&). What happens to the second insert?
options: It fails: the ranges touch at 10:00
It succeeds: half-open ranges that only touch don't overlap
quiz.why: The first range excludes 10:00 itself, so && is false and the constraint is satisfied.

quiz.q: Why does `EXCLUDE USING gist (room WITH =, during WITH &&)` with room text need btree_gist?
options: GiST has no built-in operator class for = on text
quiz.why: Ranges have GiST support built in; btree_gist supplies GiST operator classes for scalar types like text and int.

further_reading.title: PostgreSQL docs: Range Types (constraints on ranges)

body:
## Concept

A **generated column** is `GENERATED ALWAYS AS (expression)`, computed from other columns
of the same row and never written directly. PG 12 introduced the **STORED** kind,
computed on write and kept on disk. PG 18 adds **VIRTUAL**, computed on read with no
storage, and makes it the default. The expression may use only immutable functions and
the current row.

An **exclusion constraint** generalizes UNIQUE: for any two rows, comparing them with the
listed operators must not return true for all of them. UNIQUE is the special case where
every operator is `=`. With `&&` (overlaps) on a range column, "no double booking"
becomes a constraint, and a `WHERE` clause can limit it to some rows.

## Coming from C/C++/Java/Python/JS

- Python/TS: a virtual column is a `@property` or getter, computed on access. A stored
  column is a field that the database recomputes on every write, so it can never go stale.
- Java/Go: a computed field on an entity or struct only exists in that one program. A
  generated column gives the same value to every reader, including SQL reports.
- Overlap checks in application code (load the bookings of that room, compare intervals,
  insert) race under concurrency, much like an unlocked check-then-act on a shared map.
  The exclusion constraint is checked through its index and holds across transactions.

## Design notes

Choose the kind by how the value is used. Virtual suits values that are cheap to compute
and rarely filtered on; it adds nothing to writes or disk. Stored suits values you index,
search or sort by, or that are expensive to compute, at the price of storage and write
time.

PG 18 also adds temporal keys: `PRIMARY KEY (room, during WITHOUT OVERLAPS)` behaves like
`EXCLUDE USING gist (room WITH =, during WITH &&)` and needs btree_gist for the same
reason. Reach for plain EXCLUDE when you need what a key can't express: a `WHERE`
clause, as with cancelled bookings, or operators other than `=` and `&&`. The temporal
data lesson covers WITHOUT OVERLAPS and PERIOD foreign keys.

files.examples/01_generated.sql:
-- LEARN(sql.constraints.generated): derived values the application cannot get wrong.
CREATE TABLE products (
  id          int  PRIMARY KEY,
  name        text NOT NULL,
  net_cents   int  NOT NULL,
  vat_pct     int  NOT NULL DEFAULT 20,
  -- No keyword: VIRTUAL in PG 18. Computed on read, takes no space on disk.
  gross_cents int GENERATED ALWAYS AS (net_cents * (100 + vat_pct) / 100),
  -- STORED: computed on INSERT/UPDATE and written like a normal column.
  name_key    text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (lower(name)) STORED
);

INSERT INTO products (id, name, net_cents) VALUES
  (1, 'Iğdır kayısısı', 4500),
  (2, 'İzmir inciri', 12000);
UPDATE products SET vat_pct = 10 WHERE id = 2;   -- gross_cents follows

SELECT id, name, name_key, net_cents, vat_pct, gross_cents
FROM products
ORDER BY id;

-- attgenerated: 's' = stored, 'v' = virtual.
SELECT attname, attgenerated
FROM pg_attribute
WHERE attrelid = 'products'::regclass AND attgenerated <> ''
ORDER BY attnum;

CREATE INDEX ON products (name_key);      -- stored: indexable
CREATE INDEX ON products (gross_cents);   -- virtual: not in PG 18
files.examples/03_per_room.sql:
-- = on a plain column inside a GiST index needs btree_gist. It is a trusted
-- extension: the database owner can install it without being a superuser.
CREATE EXTENSION btree_gist;

CREATE TABLE bookings (
  id        int  PRIMARY KEY,
  room      text NOT NULL,
  during    tsrange NOT NULL,
  cancelled boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  -- Same room AND overlapping time is forbidden, among live bookings only.
  CONSTRAINT bookings_room_no_overlap
    EXCLUDE USING gist (room WITH =, during WITH &&) WHERE (NOT cancelled)
);

INSERT INTO bookings (id, room, during) VALUES
  (1, 'Galata',    '[2026-11-13 09:00, 2026-11-13 10:00)'),
  (2, 'Bosphorus', '[2026-11-13 09:00, 2026-11-13 10:00)');  -- other room
UPDATE bookings SET cancelled = true WHERE id = 1;
INSERT INTO bookings (id, room, during) VALUES
  (3, 'Galata',    '[2026-11-13 09:30, 2026-11-13 10:30)');  -- slot was freed

SELECT id, room, during, cancelled
FROM bookings
ORDER BY room, lower(during), id;

INSERT INTO bookings (id, room, during) VALUES
  (4, 'Galata',    '[2026-11-13 10:00, 2026-11-13 11:00)');
